summary_oneline: Add `parrot self migration`: a packaged, ledger-tracked, versioned schema-migration runner for parrot-owned tables, starting with navigator.ai_bots, modelled on navauth self upgrade.

localization.role: click group `parrot self` (managed runtime ~/.parrot); the new `migration` verb is one more lazily-imported command here
readiness checks with fix hints; natural home for a read-only 'pending schema migrations' row
root LazyGroup registry (`self` → parrot.self_.cli); supports commands implemented in satellite distributions with install hints
strict asyncdb model of navigator.ai_bots (49 fields, Meta.strict=True): target schema; a missing column breaks every bot load
compat shim tolerating pre-fold databases — evidence that environments sit at unknown schema versions
destructive bootstrap DDL (DROP … CASCADE at line 9) with hand-appended ALTERs; already missing FEAT-752 columns
idempotent additive catch-up script (Status: pending), candidate seed for a baseline migration
de-facto file convention: own BEGIN/COMMIT, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, rollback in comments, deploy-order prose
15 loose, unpackaged, unordered hand-run SQL files (8 ai_bots schema + data fixes + planogram/ontology domain data)
existing parrot ledger runner (navigator.ai_studio_migrations, console script parrot-studio-migrate) scoped to Agent Studio tables
runtime DSN from DB* settings; no admin/DDL DSN exists
configurable schema/table names (PARROT_SCHEMA, PARROT_BOTS_TABLE) — SQL must be templated
third in-repo pattern: startup version check + explicit apply_migrations at deploy
byte-freeze gate on creation.sql + BotModel docstring DDL; edits need a _SANCTIONED_REWRITES entry
reference runner: (set, filename) sha256 ledger, session advisory lock, one transaction per file, continue-on-failure
reference catalog: sql/<set>/NNN_*.sql discovery, ordered MIGRATION_SETS, render_sql placeholders
reference CLI: navauth self upgrade --check/--dsn/--user/--set/--fail-fast, exit codes 0-3
reference startup behaviour: read-only warning, never DDL
test home for the new CLI verb

constraints.statement: BotModel is strict: every declared field is selected by name, so a column the code expects but the table lacks fails every bot load.
constraints.implication: migrations must run before deploying code that adds fields; a model-vs-DB column check is high value

constraints.statement: creation.sql is a destructive bootstrap (DROP TABLE … CASCADE) whose constraint/trigger statements are not idempotent and which lacks the FEAT-752 columns.
constraints.implication: it cannot be reused as a migration; the baseline must be rewritten as guarded, additive SQL

constraints.statement: creation.sql and the BotModel docstring DDL are byte-frozen by test_storage_gates (test_load_database_bots_untouched / _SANCTIONED_REWRITES).
constraints.implication: any edit that points them at the new command must be registered as a sanctioned rewrite

constraints.statement: Schema and table names are configurable (PARROT_SCHEMA, PARROT_BOTS_TABLE) but every existing SQL file hard-codes navigator.ai_bots.
constraints.implication: migration SQL must use placeholders rendered from config, as navauth's render_sql does

constraints.statement: sdd/migrations/ is outside every distribution, so an installed parrot cannot read it; navauth decided SQL lives in-package.
constraints.implication: the catalog must ship as package data (importlib.resources), like Studio's migrations

constraints.statement: The ai_bots DDL ships from ai-parrot-server while BotModel and the self_ CLI are in core.
constraints.implication: either the bots set lives in core next to BotModel, or the core CLI discovers sets contributed by installed satellites

constraints.statement: asyncdb execute() returns errors instead of raising; navauth's runner therefore uses a raw asyncpg connection and execute_checked.
constraints.implication: the parrot runner must not trust asyncdb execute() results for recording a file as applied

constraints.statement: Existing ai_bots scripts open and close their own transaction (BEGIN/COMMIT) and keep rollback DDL in comments.
constraints.implication: importing them into a per-file-transaction runner requires stripping BEGIN/COMMIT

constraints.statement: Parrot already has a ledger table in the navigator schema (navigator.ai_studio_migrations) with different semantics (integer versions, body checksum, xact lock, MANIFEST).
constraints.implication: a second ledger must be a deliberate decision (separate vs unified), not an accident

constraints.statement: Startup must never run DDL: navauth warns only, Studio never migrates at startup, task-memory verifies and refuses.
constraints.implication: startup/doctor integration is read-only (warn on pending)

constraints.statement: parrot conf has no admin/DDL credential; only the runtime default_dsn.
constraints.implication: add an optional admin DSN setting with fallback to default_dsn and a notice, mirroring navauth's precedence

constraints.statement: `parrot self` is scoped to the managed runtime, `self update` already exists, and `migrate_legacy_uv` already uses the word migration inside self_.
constraints.implication: the verb name and help text must disambiguate DB schema migration from runtime/uv migration

new: A core migrations package (catalog + runner + status/ledger models), modelled on navauth: sql/<set>/NNN_<name>.sql files shipped as package data, ordered sets, sha256 checksums, APPLIED/PENDING/CHANGED states, advisory lock, one transaction per file, Pydantic report
A parrot-owned ledger table in PARROT_SCHEMA keyed by (migration_set, filename)

A `bots` migration set for navigator.ai_bots: guarded baseline derived from ai-bots-homologate-botmodel.sql + FEAT-752 columns, then the fold steps in git-date order, all templated with {schema}/{bots_table}
`parrot self migration` CLI verb(s): status/--check, upgrade, --set, --dsn, --fail-fast, exit codes 0 ok / 1 pending / 2 failed / 3 config
Read-only pending-migrations check in `parrot self doctor` and a startup warning where BotManager loads database bots
A documented convention (docs/migrations/) and a consistency test that the bots set covers every BotModel column

modified.change: register the `migration` command/group (lazy import of the runner)
add an optional admin DSN setting used by the runner, falling back to default_dsn
point operators to the command (sanctioned rewrite) or demote to fresh-install-only
retire the ai_bots scripts once folded into the packaged set

untouched: Data migrations and non-parrot domain data (planogram, ecotank, ontology seeds in sdd/migrations/)
Tables that self-create at runtime with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (ui_surfaces, crew_definitions, …) in v1
External migration tools (alembic etc.) and non-Postgres databases

patterns.pattern: navauth FEAT-110 design: catalog/runner/checks/startup/cli split, sets, (set, filename) ledger, --check, exit codes, admin-DSN precedence, sanitized errors
Studio runner: importlib.resources package data, concurrent-runner safety, --print for DBAs, file-only tests + live-DB tests that skip when Postgres is unreachable
LazyGroup registration with lazy imports and install hints for satellite-provided commands

risks.risk: Two ledgers in the navigator schema (ai_studio_migrations + the new one) with diverging semantics
risks.mitigation: decide in the spec: keep Studio separate, or absorb it as a set

risks.risk: Pre-existing databases at unknown versions with scripts partially hand-applied; fold scripts DROP columns
risks.mitigation: idempotent guarded SQL (IF EXISTS / IF NOT EXISTS) so a first run is a no-op where already applied; keep _fold_legacy_bot_columns until all environments report clean

risks.risk: Runtime DB user may lack DDL rights
risks.mitigation: admin DSN option with fallback and notice

risks.risk: self_ is a high-churn installer package
risks.mitigation: keep the runner in its own module; touch self_/cli.py only to register the verb
register a _SANCTIONED_REWRITES entry for any edit

confidence_map.reasoning: direct reads of cli.py and cli/__init__.py

confidence_map.reasoning: grep + read of both files, citations probe-verified

confidence_map.statement: creation.sql is destructive, partly non-idempotent and already drifted (no FEAT-752 columns), so it cannot serve as a migration.
confidence_map.reasoning: DROP at line 9 verified; grep count of enable_suggestions = 0

confidence_map.statement: ai_bots schema changes are tracked only by hand-run loose SQL in sdd/migrations/ (15 files, 8 ai_bots schema), unpackaged, unordered and without a ledger.
confidence_map.reasoning: git ls-files count and per-file inspection

confidence_map.statement: Deployed environments sit at unknown ai_bots schema versions (fold migrations pending on staging/prod).
confidence_map.reasoning: stated in commit 4f05450930 and by the compat shim; no live DB was inspected

confidence_map.statement: navauth self upgrade = catalog of sql/<set>/NNN files + (set, filename) sha256 ledger + session advisory lock + per-file transaction + --check + exit codes 0-3 + admin-DSN precedence + read-only startup warning; no rollback and no baseline flag.
confidence_map.reasoning: spec and code read; citations verified

confidence_map.statement: Parrot already ships a ledger-based migration runner for Agent Studio (navigator.ai_studio_migrations, parrot-studio-migrate) that does not cover ai_bots.
confidence_map.reasoning: migrate.py read, console script in server pyproject

confidence_map.statement: Parrot has at least four independent schema mechanisms (Studio runner, task-memory verify/apply, runtime CREATE IF NOT EXISTS, loose SQL).
Runtime self-created tables handle creation but not column evolution, so they share ai_bots' drift risk.
confidence_map.reasoning: about 70 of 163 CREATE TABLE sites inspected

confidence_map.statement: parrot conf has no admin/DDL DSN setting.
Migration SQL must be templated because schema and table names are configurable.
Migration SQL must ship inside a package; sdd/ is not in any wheel.
creation.sql and the BotModel docstring DDL are byte-frozen by a test gate requiring sanctioned rewrites.
confidence_map.reasoning: from a wiki lesson naming the test; the test file exists but the symbol was not read

confidence_map.statement: The verb name risks confusion with `self update` and the existing `migrate_legacy_uv` vocabulary in self_.
confidence_map.reasoning: names verified; impact on users is a judgement

confidence_map.statement: Neither `parrot setup` nor `parrot install` provisions database tables today.
confidence_map.reasoning: absence grep scoped to two core packages

confidence_map.statement: A version chain for ai_bots can be reconstructed from the git dates of the sdd/migrations files.
confidence_map.reasoning: order inferred from first-commit dates; some files were edited after creation

confidence_map.statement: The runner must not rely on asyncdb execute() to detect failure.
confidence_map.reasoning: documented gotcha with code (execute_checked) in navauth

confidence_map.statement: The ai_bots DDL ships from ai-parrot-server while BotModel and the CLI are core, so set placement/discovery is a design decision.

unknowns.question: Which runner should `parrot self migration` build on: a new navauth-style runner (sets + (set, filename) ledger), or a generalisation of Studio's existing parrot-studio-migrate runner (integer versions, MANIFEST)?
plausible_answers: New navauth-style runner; Studio keeps its own ledger for now
New navauth-style runner; Studio becomes a set under the same ledger
Generalise Studio's runner and add ai_bots to it
unknowns.user_answer: navauth-style, Studio apart — new generic runner mirroring navauth (sets, (set, filename) ledger); Studio keeps its own ledger for now.

unknowns.question: What is the v1 scope: only navigator.ai_bots, or also other parrot-owned tables?
plausible_answers: ai_bots only, with a registry other subsystems can join later
unknowns.user_answer: ai_bots + runtime tables — also cover navigator.* tables that self-create at runtime (ui_surfaces, crew_definitions, …).

unknowns.question: How should databases that already have some or all changes applied by hand be adopted?
plausible_answers: Idempotent files only: first run re-executes and records (navauth)
Add a --baseline/--stamp that records files without running them
unknowns.user_answer: Idempotent + baseline — files stay idempotent (first run is a no-op where applied) AND a --baseline/--stamp records files without running them.

unknowns.question: What CLI shape should the command have?
plausible_answers: Group with verbs: parrot self migration status | upgrade | new
Single command like navauth: parrot self migration [--check]
Different noun outside self (e.g. parrot db migrate)
unknowns.user_answer: Group with verbs — parrot self migration status | upgrade | baseline | new (`new` scaffolds the next NNN_*.sql for a set).

unknowns.question: What happens to sdd/migrations/ and creation.sql once the packaged set exists?
plausible_answers: Move ai_bots scripts into the package set and delete them from sdd/migrations; creation.sql becomes fresh-install only, pointing to the command
Keep sdd/migrations as historical record; packaged set is a rewrite
Generate creation.sql from the migration chain
unknowns.user_answer: Move ai_bots, demote creation.sql — ai_bots scripts move into the package set (removed from sdd/migrations); planogram/ontology files stay; creation.sql becomes fresh-install only and points to the command (sanctioned rewrite).

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and the reference design is concrete; the two architectural forks (runner base U1, scope U2) are narrow binary choices captured as unknowns and settled in Q&A, so a spec can follow directly.
